short_definition: Set default file creation permissions mask
description: Displays or sets automated permission bit mask subtracted when creating new files and directories.
example_explanation: Sets default file mask ensuring new files get 644 and directories 755 permissions.
common_options: -S (symbolic output format u=rwx,g=rx,o=rx)

short_definition: Print system information
description: Prints system architecture, kernel version, hostname, and OS release information.
example_explanation: Outputs complete system details: Linux kernel version, machine architecture, build date.
common_options:
-a (print all system details)
-r (print kernel release)
-m (print machine hardware architecture)
-o (print operating system name)

short_definition: Show or set the system's host name
description: Displays or configures the network hostname of the current system.
example_explanation: Displays all network IP addresses assigned to system host.
common_options: -I (display all network host addresses)\n-f (display fully qualified domain name FQDN)\n-d (display domain name)

short_definition: Tell how long the system has been running
description: Outputs system uptime duration, count of logged in users, and 1, 5, 15 minute CPU load averages.
example_explanation: Displays system uptime duration in a friendly readable format.
common_options: -p (pretty format uptime)\n-s (since when system has been booted)

short_definition: Display amount of free and used memory in the system
description: Reports total, used, available, and swap physical RAM memory capacities.
example_explanation: Displays memory statistics in human-readable units with total aggregate row.
common_options:
-h (human-readable format GB/MB)
-m (show memory in MB)
-g (show memory in GB)
-t (display total memory summary line)

short_definition: Display information about the CPU architecture
description: Gathers CPU architecture details from sysfs and /proc/cpuinfo (cores, threads, sockets, NUMA nodes, cache).
example_explanation: Displays detailed breakdown of system processor architecture and features.
common_options: -e (extended readable CPU format)\n-J (output in JSON format)

short_definition: List USB devices
description: Inspects attached USB buses and connected device hardware details.
example_explanation: Displays verbose details for connected Apple USB devices.
common_options: -v (verbose output)\n-t (dump physical USB device hierarchy tree)\n-d vendor:product (filter by device IDs)

short_definition: List all PCI devices
description: Lists hardware controllers and expansion cards connected to PCI/PCIe bus (GPU, NVMe controllers, WiFi cards).
example_explanation: Displays graphics card hardware model alongside bound kernel drivers.
common_options: -nn (show numerical vendor and device codes)\n-k (show kernel drivers handling device)\n-v (verbose output)

short_definition: Control the systemd system and service manager
description: Primary utility for managing systemd services, targets, sockets, and system state.
example_explanation: Checks active running state and recent logs of Nginx service.
common_options:
start / stop / restart / reload
enable (enable service at boot)
disable (disable boot autostart)
is-active / is-enabled

short_definition: Query the systemd journal logs
description: Fetches, filters, and streams log messages indexed by systemd journald daemon.
example_explanation: Follows Docker service log output streaming last 50 entries.
common_options:
-u service (filter by systemd unit)
-f (follow live log stream)
-n lines (number of journal entries)
-b (logs from current boot only)
--since "1 hour ago"

short_definition: Daemon to execute scheduled commands
description: Background daemon responsible for triggering periodic cron jobs configured in crontabs.
example_explanation: Runs main cron scheduling service.
common_options: -f (run daemon in foreground mode)

short_definition: Maintain crontab files for individual users
description: Schedules automated recurring background tasks using cron timetable syntax.
syntax: crontab [-u user] file or crontab [-u user] [-e | -l | -r]
example_explanation: Opens interactive editor to configure user recurring cron jobs.
common_options:
-e (edit active crontab file)
-l (list active user crontab jobs)
-r (remove active crontab file)
-u user (manage crontab for specified user)

short_definition: Print effective user name
description: Outputs the username associated with the active effective user ID.
example_explanation: Prints current logged-in username (e.g., root or apple).
common_options: --help (display help manual)

short_definition: Print real and effective user and group IDs
description: Outputs user ID (UID), primary group ID (GID), and secondary group memberships for specified user.
example_explanation: Displays UID and group IDs assigned to www-data account.
common_options:
-u (print only effective user ID)
-g (print only primary group ID)
-G (print all secondary group IDs)
-n (print names instead of numbers)

short_definition: Show who is logged on and what they are doing
description: Displays active logged-in user sessions, login times, IP origins, and running shell commands.
example_explanation: Prints active terminal session list with CPU load stats.
common_options: -h (do not print header)\n-s (short format output)

short_definition: Create a new user or update default new user information
description: Low-level utility to create new system user account records.
example_explanation: Creates user devuser with home directory and default bash shell.
common_options:
-m (create user home directory)
-s shell (specify default login shell)
-g group (primary group)
-G groups (supplementary groups list)

short_definition: Modify a user account
description: Updates existing user account properties like group membership, home directory, and shell.
example_explanation: Appends user devuser to supplementary group docker.
common_options:
-aG groups (append supplementary groups)
-s shell (change default login shell)
-L (lock user password)
-U (unlock user account)

short_definition: Change user password
description: Updates account authentication passwords in /etc/shadow.
example_explanation: Prompts for new password for user devuser.
common_options: -l (lock user password)\n-u (unlock user password)\n-e (expire password forcing user change at next login)

short_definition: Command-line package manager for Debian/Ubuntu
description: High-level interface for installing, updating, searching, and removing software packages on Debian/Ubuntu systems.
example: sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y build-essential
example_explanation: Updates package index repositories and installs C/C++ compilation tools.
common_options:
update (fetch latest package lists)
upgrade (upgrade all installed packages)
install pkg (install package)
remove pkg (remove package)
search query (search repository packages)

short_definition: Debian package manager
description: Low-level Debian software package tool for installing and inspecting local .deb binary files.
example_explanation: Installs downloaded Google Chrome Debian package file.
common_options:
-i file.deb (install package)
-r pkg (remove package)
-l pattern (list installed packages matching pattern)
-L pkg (list files installed by package)

short_definition: Arch Linux package manager utility
description: Fast package manager for Arch Linux handling dependency resolution and package building.
example_explanation: Synchronizes package databases, upgrades system, and installs neovim editor.
common_options:
-Syu (sync repos and upgrade system)
-Ss pattern (search package repos)
-R pkg (remove package)
-Q (query installed packages)

short_definition: Next-generation Fedora package manager
description: Package manager for Fedora, RHEL, and CentOS managing RPM packages.
example_explanation: Installs PostgreSQL database server on Fedora/RHEL system.
common_options:
install pkg (install package)
update / upgrade (upgrade packages)
search query (search packages)
remove pkg (uninstall package)

short_definition: GNU Compiler Collection for C/C++
description: Compiles and links C/C++ source code files into executable binary programs.
example_explanation: Compiles main.c with optimization level 2 and warnings enabled producing app binary.
common_options:
-O2 / -O3 (optimization level)
-Wall (enable all compiler warnings)
-g (generate debug symbols for gdb)
-o outfile (output binary path)

short_definition: Distributed version control system
description: Tracks source code changes, manages branches, and handles distributed repository operations.
example_explanation: Displays last 10 repository commits in single-line summary format.
common_options: status / add / commit / push / pull / checkout / branch / log / diff / clone / merge

short_definition: GNU make utility to maintain groups of programs
description: Automates compilation of source code targets guided by Makefiles.
example_explanation: Runs Makefile target "build" executing 4 parallel compilation jobs.
common_options: -j jobs (number of parallel build jobs)\n-f file (use specified Makefile path)\n-C dir (change to directory before reading Makefile)

short_definition: Vi IMproved - text editor
description: Highly configurable terminal-based modal text editor designed for fast code editing.
example_explanation: Opens index.js directly positioned at line 25.
common_options: -R (read-only mode)\n-b (binary mode)\n+line (jump to line number on open)

short_definition: Simple command line text editor
description: Easy-to-use, beginner-friendly terminal text editor with visible shortcut keys.
example_explanation: Opens /etc/hosts file with mouse support enabled.
common_options: -m (enable mouse support)\n-B (create backup copies on edit)\n-N (enable line numbers)

short_definition: OpenSSL command line tool for cryptography
description: Cryptography toolkit for SSL/TLS certificates generation, encryption algorithms, and key management.
example_explanation: Decodes and displays SSL certificate expiration dates and Subject fields.
common_options:
req (generate certificate signing request CSR)
x509 (manage certificates)
rand -hex n (generate random bytes)
enc (encrypt/decrypt data)

short_definition: OpenPGP encryption and signing tool
description: Encrypts files, verifies cryptographic signatures, and manages PGP keyrings.
example_explanation: Encrypts secret.txt with password using AES256 cipher producing secret.txt.gpg.
common_options:
-c / --symmetric (encrypt with passphrase)
-d (decrypt file)
-k (list keys)
--import file (import PGP key)

short_definition: Compute and check SHA256 message digest
description: Computes SHA-256 cryptographic hash digest of input files to verify integrity.
example_explanation: Verifies SHA256 checksum of ISO image against hash file.
common_options: -c (check checksums against file)\n-b (read files in binary mode)\n-t (read files in text mode)

short_definition: Compute and check MD5 message digest
description: Computes 128-bit MD5 checksum hash for file integrity validation.
example_explanation: Outputs 32-character hexadecimal MD5 hash of release.zip.
common_options: -c (check checksum file)\n-b (read binary files)

short_definition: Display or set system date and time
description: Displays current date and time in custom formats or sets system clock.
example_explanation: Outputs formatted timestamp string (e.g. 2026-09-20 20:30:00).
common_options: +FORMAT (custom format string specifiers %Y, %m, %d, %H, %M, %S, %s epoch)\n-u (display UTC time)\n-d string (parse custom date string)

short_definition: Display a calendar
description: Displays a formatted monthly or yearly calendar grid in the terminal.
example_explanation: Displays calendar grid for previous, current, and next month around September 2026.
common_options: -3 (display 3 months)\n-y (display full current year calendar)\n-j (display julian days)

short_definition: Delay for a specified amount of time
description: Pauses execution for a specified duration in seconds, minutes, hours, or days.
example_explanation: Pauses execution for 5 seconds before printing message.
common_options:
s (seconds)
m (minutes)
h (hours)
d (days)
